sourceChecks.claim: Live CoreComponents identifies unique primary keys and direct retrieval. Cache/authoritative role distinction is consistent with Redis eviction documentation; Redis persistence followup https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/persistence/ confirms configurable persistence and possible data loss, supporting the absence of inherent durability.

Live GetItem distinguishes a matching item from a successful no-Item response and documents selected read consistency. ConditionalExpressions live followup confirms PutItem overwrites an existing same-key item; transaction-apis confirms Delete removes the keyed item. A missing response cannot establish the successful absent response.

Live IAM conditions page requires policies tied to user identity and item keys: naming a key alone does not confer permission. Composite identity examples in CoreComponents support unique identity; the separator warning follows from ambiguous concatenation. The assigned organization diagram keeps access checks separate.

Live SecondaryIndexes documents alternate lookup keys, copied base keys, automatic maintenance, update capacity and differing read consistency. Live followup https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Scan.html confirms filtering happens after reads and does not reduce consumed read capacity.

Live ConditionExpressions permits mutation only when its condition holds. Live https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DynamoDBMapper.OptimisticLocking.html confirms version mismatch rejects updates and requires rereading. Under the stated atomic condition-and-mutation boundary, one old-version update succeeds; separate checks cannot provide that guarantee.

Live Programming.Errors says a failed write response may mask success and distinguishes retryable errors. Live https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/transaction-apis.html confirms atomic write groups and identity-token deduplication, a finite token window, and rejection of changed intent. This supports same-identity retries only within verified mechanism scope; atomic increments alone do not deduplicate.

Live TTL documents background deletion after expiration, pending expired items and filtering. Live https://redis.io/docs/latest/develop/reference/eviction/ confirms capacity-triggered configurable eviction including keys with remaining TTL. Neither document promises refresh or exact-time business execution; retention is not established by TTL.

Live partition-key guidance describes distributing activity and per-partition/item limits, supporting the qualified hot-key warning. Live https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadConsistency.html explicitly separates durable acknowledged writes from eventually consistent stale reads and documents read-mode differences.

Live NoSQL-design guide requires identifying access patterns and data size/shape/velocity, notes expensive access outside supported patterns and warns about concentrated traffic. This supports workload-specific choice and measurement rather than universal speed or safety.
